title: Slimline SDK first-commit checklist and quickstart
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, opinionated checklist for an engineer shipping the very first commit that integrates the Redwood SDK into a sample app or service. The goal is to get a minimal, usable integration with safe defaults, basic telemetry, and CI smoke checks in place within 1–2 hours.

Scope and audience:
- For: engineers doing first-time SDK integration (internal demos, POCs, sample apps)
- Not for: full production rollout (see rollout playbooks)
- Priority: speed + observability + sensible safety defaults

Quick decision rules (read before starting):
- If you need an advanced feature (sidecar, private deployment), skip this and follow the dedicated onboarding doc
- Keep the first commit tiny: one sample endpoint, one test, one telemetry metric, and one CI check

Pre-commit checklist (local dev):
1) Repo setup
   - Fork or branch from main: git checkout -b devexp/sdk-first-commit-<yourname>
   - Add a short README note describing the sample endpoint and how to run locally
2) Minimal dependency installation
   - Add the SDK dependency only (npm/pip/go mod): example: npm i @redwood-inference/sdk --save
   - Add a lightweight wrapper (helper.js): exports.redwoodClient = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: process.env.REDWOOD_REGION || 'us-west-2' });
3) Environment variables (local):
   - Create .env.local with placeholders (do not check in secrets):
     REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_test_xxx
     REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
   - Document where to get test key (link to internal vault or dev portal)
4) Security quick wins
   - Ensure no secrets are committed (git status + git grep to check for REDWOOD_API_KEY)
   - Add .env.local to .gitignore if not already present

First-commit contents (what to include in a minimal PR):
- One tiny sample route/handler that calls the SDK and returns text (or structured JSON). Keep model output length small.
- A basic unit/integration test that mocks the SDK call and asserts the handler returns expected shape.
- A single telemetry metric emitted locally (see telemetry below).
- A short README snippet with run and test commands.
- A CI job stub that will run the test and the linter.

Minimal sample handler (pseudocode):
- POST /api/generate -> calls redwoodClient.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: 'Summarize: ' + req.body.text, max_tokens: 80 }) -> return { summary: response.text }
Notes: pick a small curated model to limit costs in CI/sample runs.

CI and gating (fast feedback):
- Add a single lightweight CI job (name: sdk-smoke) that runs:
  - install deps, run unit tests
  - run a smoke test that uses a local mock (do not call hosted API from CI by default)
  - enforce no secrets in the PR (custom script: scripts/check-no-secrets.sh)
- Consider an optional nightly job that exercises the real hosted API using a short credit bucket (feature-flagged)

Telemetry and observability (minimal):
- Emit one request counter and one latency histogram for the sample route:
  - metric names: sdk.sample_request.count, sdk.sample_request.latency_ms
- Tag with: team=devexp, env=test, sample=true, model=redwood-small
- For the first commit, push telemetry to the low-cost dev metrics project (point to internal metrics endpoint, not prod)
- Add a single log line for the upstream SDK response with a low-sensitivity redact policy (do not log user content). Example: logger.info('redwood: model=redwood-small tokens=42 latency_ms=123');

Error handling and safety defaults:
- Default to a 3s network timeout for SDK calls in sample code
- Fail gracefully: on SDK error return { error: 'service_unavailable' } with 502 rather than leaking stack traces
- Simple rate-limiting note: wrap the handler with a token-bucket guard in comments (point to full-rate-limit playbook)

Testing matrix (keep tiny):
- unit: mocks for SDK call (node: jest with nock or python: pytest + monkeypatch)
- integration: local run using recorded fixture (avoid live API)
- smoke: CI job runs unit + lint; optional nightly triggers live call under feature flag

PR checklist (to paste into PR description):
- [ ] Branch name follows pattern devexp/sdk-first-commit-<name>
- [ ] README contains run/test steps and env var guidance
- [ ] Tests added + passing locally
- [ ] Telemetry metric emitted and documented in README
- [ ] Secrets scanning passed (scripts/check-no-secrets.sh)
- [ ] Small scope: single endpoint, single test, single CI job

Local debugging tips:
- Use a local mock server for SDK responses (example: npm run redwood-mock)
- Set VERBOSE_SDK_LOGS=true for a short time to capture call/response timing (do not enable on shared dev infra)
- Use curl to exercise the endpoint: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/generate -d '{"text":"notes from meeting"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Known gotchas (short):
- default token limit in example configs may be too large; keep max_tokens <= 120 for initial commits
- CI should not use real API keys; if you must, gate behind an allowlist and short-lived token
- Telemetry metric names should be validated with metrics platform team to avoid collisions

Next steps after first commit (follow-up items to track in a separate ticket):
- Add proper retry/backoff for production patterns
- Add model selection config + knob to switch between curated models
- Expand test coverage: contract tests + e2e using a dedicated dev credits bucket
- Add a runbook linking errors to remediation steps and who to page

References and internal links:
- Internal example app: github.com/redwood-inference/examples/simple-chat (link in linked_artifacts)
- Dev Slack: #devexp-sdk-onboard
- Rollout playbook: CONFLUENCE-REDWOOD-SDK-ROLLOUT

Loose timeline suggestion for an engineer: 0–30m: repo + deps + .env; 30–75m: sample handler + test + README; 75–120m: CI job + telemetry + PR polish.

Notes to reviewers (short):
- This is intentionally minimal and opinionated. Please review for safety holes and for any hard-coded defaults that should be moved to config.
- If we accept, this document becomes the canonical "first commit" checklist and should be linked from SDK quickstarts and bootcamp labs.

Author notes:
- Priya (devexp) — initial draft. Marco and Aisha + SRE reviewed error/telemetry sections.
